subject: lizard
readings: head at -x: XY panel is the profile (nose-tail = x, dorsal-ventral = y); XZ panel is the top view (x nose-tail, z = left-right splay); ZY panel is the front view (z width, y height)
snout tip (0,11) to neck junction (9,11) in XY panel: head length ~9
torso mid/root (13,11) to neck junction (9,11) in XY panel: neck length ~4
root (13,11) to hip (17,12) in XY panel: torso-to-hip offset ~4, hip sits slightly lower (ground-ward) than root
hip (17,12) to tail tip (24,12) in XY panel: tail length ~7
front leg shoulder attach ~x=9,y=12 in XY panel; in XZ panel front legs splay from centerline z=12 out to z≈2 (left) and z≈22 (right), giving strong lateral component
hind leg hip attach ~x=17,y=12 in XY panel; in XZ panel hind legs splay similarly from z=12 to z≈2 (left) and z≈22 (right)
leg vertical drop in XY panel from shoulder/hip line (y≈12) to foot line (y≈16-17): ~4-5 units, split across two joints (shoulder/elbow, hip/knee) since limbs bend once visibly in the render
notes: Lizard has a fused-looking short neck (inferred as a small segment between root and head since XY shows a continuous rounded head/neck mass). Tail treated as single segment root(hip)->tip since no visible joint. Each leg split into two segments (upper limb + lower limb) based on the visible bend in the XY panel silhouette and the strong lateral splay seen in the XZ (top) panel; the z-component of leg directions is inferred from the XZ panel's leg spread since the XY panel alone only shows the vertical/forward-back component. Left/right assigned by animal's own orientation (viewer's right in the panels = animal's left, since XY shows the belly/side with head at -x, so pairs are named _L/_R by mirrored z-sign). Root placed at a neutral mid-torso point (13,11,12) purely for computing relative directions; only directions matter, not absolute position.
